actual_findings: The public wrapper first tries fmpz_lll_d, checks reducedness, then selects a heuristic double stage or fmpz_lll_mpf fallback according to the context. This is adaptive arithmetic, so our rational GMP prototype cannot be labelled the fastest specialized reducer.

Reducedness checking for integer bases strips initial zero rows and tries double, MPFR and exact matrix checks. This is implementation evidence, not an independent benchmark or mathematical novelty certification.

Our lifted-mask soundness needs exact modular membership and range replay, not a particular LLL quality guarantee. A faster numerical discovery arm can therefore be tried with exact final certificate checking and complete recovery of every unexcluded fiber.
classical_overlap: Integer dual lattices, unimodular basis changes, adaptive numerical LLL and exact final checks are known techniques. No novelty claim for these components. Full primary-literature review of the chart-specific construction remains open.
next_bounded_experiment: Pin a genuine external FLINT/fplll binary/library and public context, then compare discovery-plus-replay-plus-complete survivor union to exact rational4D/7D on a newly fixed training ladder. Retain all failed arms; no arbitrary warm timeout retry.
